title: Patanjali — Risk & Reputation Research
content:
The sources indicate that Patanjali Ayurved Limited has faced customer complaints and negative reviews. One review on REVIEWS.io mentions poor service and a missing item despite prepaid order, with no response from Patanjali. Another source on YouTube discusses allegations of misleading advertisements, poor product quality, and low wages paid to talent, though it notes that some claims, like the use of animal contents in products, were allegations rather than confirmed facts. Patanjali Ayurved Limited's grievance redressal policy is managed by Fit India Organic Private Limited, which aims to resolve customer issues within 7 working days.

According to The Wire, Patanjali faced supply chain issues that affected deliveries, which Balkrishna attributed to rapid expansion and network problems. Patanjali's operational challenges included poor quality management and customer service ratings, as noted in Patanjali's Operational Challenges Explained. The company's shipping policy on Patanjaliayurved.net mentions that delivery can be delayed due to unavoidable circumstances and location coverage issues, and that no early delivery is available. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on current delivery delays or service quality issues.

The 46-year-old Balkrishna, whose net worth Forbes puts at $4.9 billion, brushed aside concerns about the company's health during an April interview at one of Patanjali's yoga centres near Haridwar.

"We suddenly expanded, we started three-four new units, and so problems were expected. We have solved that network problem," said Balkrishna, referring to supply chain issues that affected deliveries. The problems were concentrated in "set-up and networking", he said, without elaborating. [...] As Patanjali has ramped up its offering to more than 2,500 goods, it has prioritised scale over quality and farmed out production to third parties, which has dented quality, two former office executives and a supplier said. [...] Some unpaid suppliers are turning their backs on the company, according to interviews with three suppliers as well as letters, reviewed by Reuters, sent to the company by those owed money.

A chemical supplier said Patanjali started delaying payments by a month or two in 2017. By 2018, delays had grown to almost six months.

Patanjali faced several operational challenges that hindered its growth, including a lack of innovation in developing new products, reduced advertising spending, ignoring competition from rivals who were launching similar natural products, poor quality management that led to product recalls, difficulties complying with new regulations, and poor customer service ratings. These issues caused Patanjali's sales and market share to decline in recent years.

The legal case against Patanjali Ayurveda, initiated by the Indian Medical Association (IMA) in August 2022, has been a significant focal point in India. The case accuses Patanjali and its founders of making false claims against evidence-based modern medicine and its practitioners, particularly through misleading advertisements claiming the effectiveness of Ayurvedic products against chronic diseases. In February 2024, the Supreme Court delivered a ruling imposing a temporary ban on Patanjali from advertising specific products that claim to treat diseases and warned against making negative statements about conventional medicine. The court also expressed exasperation with the company's lack of compliance and repeated apologies. The Uttarakhand government filed a criminal complaint against Patanjali, its managing director, and Baba Ramdev, only after repeated strictures from the Supreme Court.

The court also directed district authorities to take action against the brand if it failed to improve the quality of its products after some essential commodities like salt, jam, oil and honey, had failed quality tests.

Patanjali has faced significant reputation problems and criticism, including being embroiled in court cases with state governments, having terrible quality issues, and many of their products coming under fire for misleading claims. The company's revenue dropped by 10% and profits by nearly 50% from 2017 to 2018, and their numbers have been stagnating since. Additionally, some Patanjali product advertisements violated ASCI codes and were fined for harmful practices, and there were concerns about promoting negative sentiments in advertising.
